page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-16GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration provides 8 shared vCPUs with 8 physical cores and 1.0 thread per core, paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core capabilities alongside weaker single-core and memory bandwidth metrics. The server achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 6000.74 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6083.0, whereas its stress-ng single-core performance registered at 781.19. Memory bandwidth tests show a sharp contrast between cached small-block reads at 825.47 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 30.23 GB/sec. Similarly, the PassMark memory score of 1699.21 falls into the bottom 25% tier.

Given the shared CPU allocation and weak single-core performance, this server is positioned as a budget-friendly option for workloads that can tolerate resource sharing. It is suitable for multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation, text processing, and basic database operations, as evidenced by its average Geekbench clang compilation score of 9302.0 and PassMark database operations score of 4690.46. However, it is less optimal for high-throughput static web serving or intensive large-model LLM inference, where it exhibits weaker performance.
